purpose: Independent SF SE.03 source values and declared nominal construction defaults; thermal checks calculate forward from dimensions and retained material properties.

wall.selection: Period timber cross-frame representative: shared 12 mm porous wood-fibre windboard outside the retained 145 mm main frame, 50 mm insulated inside cross-frame and 13 mm gypsum. Original cladding, battens and ventilation cavity remain unquantified project details.

source_reference.basis: BETSI 1976–1985 stock-average wall; workbook supplies no physical layer recipe. The brochure illustrates AAC without dimensions or grade. This is an independently period-supported timber alternative.

period_source.locator: Bjerking R106:1978, printed pp39–40, Figure2222b: from1965 vertical main studs plus horizontal 2-inch inside cross-framing, full mineral-wool infill, outer wind sheathing and inner board/gypsum with vapour control.
period_source.nominal_metric_interpretation: Retain the existing 145 mm late-period main-frame nominal depth. Use a 50 mm inside cross-frame, the rounded nominal interpretation of the source 2-inch cross-member. The source drawing itself specifies a 4-inch main frame; it does not establish 145 mm.

wall.framing_scope: Retained EPSM whole-wall timber bridge allowance in each layer, including framing beyond field studs. It is not simply the source stud-width/spacing ratio, and no detailed two-dimensional junction calculation is claimed.
wall.weather_skin_scope: 12mm porous wood-fibre windboard is represented in the nominal core and quantities. Original timber cladding,battens and ventilation cavity remain outside the nominal core and unquantified. Air/vapour control,fasteners and interfaces remain project details.
wall.renovation_scope: Reuse accepted SF SE.01 exterior 45/70 mm facade-wool and 22 mm wood-panel additions. Panel resistance is counted in the full nominal renovated stack; wind/cavity/ventilation and moisture corrections remain project details. The 22 mm panel and wool grade are explicit EPSM choices, not TABULA-specified products.

period_locators: Bjerking R106:1978, printedpp39–40/Fig2222b:1965-onward wall has external asphalt-impregnated porous wood-fibre windboard.
Bjerking R106:1978, printedpp87–89/Figs2613–2615:1960-onward cladding on battens over windboard, with air space.
source.nominal_dimension_scope: A current manufacturer asphalt-windboard family confirms 12 mm as a nominal board size. It is a declared representative dimension, not a recovered 1978 product specification.

modern_product_comparison.scope: Current manufacturer comparison only. No modern performance or composition is imported into the historic thermal proxy.

source.thermal_proxy_scope: Existing generic soft wood-fibre grade retained atlambda0.07,density230,specific_heat2100. Historic asphalt impregnation is a functional family assumption; exact asphalt content,mass,air/water performance and carbon factors are not established.

windboard.carbon_scope: Existing unmapped-retained-stock declaration remains. The same new baseline windboard component must remain unchanged in every renovation state. Unknown carbon factors are not zero; no hardboard/HDF substitution or invented fullA5 is allowed.

period_plausibility_cross_check.locator: Energimyndigheten ET2009:19, printed p11, original wall U by construction period
period_plausibility_cross_check.scope: Independent approximate period mean, not a layer recipe or a substitute for the fixed TABULA benchmark.

window.selection_scope: Original 2.01 and standard 0.90 definitions are retained. Advanced reuses the accepted 0.76 wood/aluminium 2+2 TABULA replacement assumption.
window.optical_scope: Whole-aperture SHGC=glazingg*(1-framefraction), with negligible opaque-frame solar gain; VT uses the same fraction. Glazing VT is an explicit EPSM default, not a TABULA measurement. External shading and angular factors are excluded.
window.carbon_scope: Boverket IDs 0104/0106 are labelled modern timber / wood-aluminium product-family proxies. They do not establish exact historic glazing or exact 2+2 manufacturing emissions.

existing.selection: Retained accepted TABULA original-period whole-window assumption; not a verified historic product.

wall_preservation.scope: Accepted shared-definition preservation guards, not historical source benchmarks.

floor.purpose: Independent source measures and declared representative assembly assumptions; no nominal layer value is inferred from TABULA effective ground U.

source.u_basis: BETSI area-weighted stock average including soil heat transfer under ISO 13370:2007(E), not material-only resistance; the underlying statistic includes at-grade slabs and basement ground floors.
betsi_locators: BETSI Energi i bebyggelsen (2010), printed p.17, U-value calculation assumptions
BETSI Energi i bebyggelsen (2010), printed pp.19–20, slab/basement-floor population and geometry assumptions
BETSI Energi i bebyggelsen (2010), printed p.166, Appendix 2, Table 8, SF 1976–1985
source.placement_scope: Brochure illustration places added insulation above the existing slab. It does not prescribe the EPSM concrete finish, its exact thickness or a complete moisture-safe floor system.
source.source_recipe_scope: TABULA supplies a synthetic BETSI average and no original material recipe; Tab.Building.Constr!AC301 explicitly records that limitation.

assembly_defaults.baseline_scope: Representative 1978 slab on ground: retain the user P04 70 mm under-slab EPS and 120 mm concrete defaults; select a 40 mm bonded cement finish instead of a 10 mm timber finish, so renovation adds insulation above mineral baseline layers. Exact depths and finish selection are EPSM defaults, not recovered TABULA layers or values fitted to effective ground U.
assembly_defaults.finish_scope: Generic HW Concrete is a shared thermal and concrete-family carbon proxy for the bonded cement finish and the new floating cementitious floor. It is not a product-specific Weber screed specification.
period_finish_locators: SOU 1944:7, printed p.157, cement-finished basement floors
BABS 1946, printed p.7, concrete floor coverings
assembly_defaults.chronology_scope: Modin and Sundberg (2012), EPS i grund, printed p.6 (PDF page 16), reports compressed mineral-wool under-slab boards as dominant in the 1970s with occasional EPS/XPS substitution. EPS below a 1978 slab is plausible but not asserted to be the majority practice. The 70 mm depth is the retained user P04 default. TABULA has no exact building year (Tab.Building!V811 blank); 1978 is a declared representative year within 1976–1985.
assembly_defaults.retained_user_recipe_locator: evidence/sfh_baseline_user_stacks.txt, SFH-P04 to SFH-P09: P04 (1971–1980) 70 mm under-slab EPS, 120 mm concrete and 10 mm timber finish; this correction explicitly changes only the floor finish of that representative recipe.

attic_preservation.scope: Pre-change physical snapshots protect shared definitions; these guards are not historical source evidence.

weather_shell.name: Representative roof weather shell
weather_shell.side_convention_note: This is the separate representative weather shell, not a complete thermal roof. The cold-attic ceiling or supplied thermal roof remains a distinct boundary.

attic_source_locators.tabula: TABULA.xlsm#'Tab.Building'!BD811,BN811,CJ811; 'Tab.Building.Constr'!I311:R311,AC311. The roof code is SE.Ceiling.ReEx.03.01, a synthetic BETSI average for 1976–1985, not a physical layer recipe. Tab.Building!V811 is blank; 1978 is an EPSM representative year.

period_context.locator: Energimyndigheten ET2009:19, printed p.11 / PDF index10, right-hand table: 1976–1985 original attic mean U0.18. The separate 1955-onwards drawing gives 100–180mm mineral wool and c/c1200, not a post-1975 depth prescription. Example U-values use an older calculation convention.

period_arrangement.locator: Bjerking R106:1978, printed p.43 / PDF index43, Figure2234 (1965 onwards): mineral-wool boards between joists, continuous mineral-wool mat above, underpanel and gypsum/wood-fibre lining. The drawing states c/c600 and joists up to3x9 inches; it does not specify the mat depths selected here.

attic_defaults.selection: Representative 1978 ceiling: retain the former nominal200mm framed depth and existing mineral-wool grade; add50mm continuous original wool following the documented over-joist arrangement. The total250mm is an explicit EPSM completion default, not a layer recipe recovered from TABULA or the ET2009:19 100–180mm illustration. The ET1976–1985 meanU0.18 is broad period-performance context, not a target used to solve a layer depth.
attic_defaults.geometry: Nominal75mm joist width at1200mm centres gives6.25% timber, reusing the declared regular-framing family selected for SFSE02. Width, spacing and50mm continuous depth are engineering defaults for this representative ceiling. The period detail supporting the over-joist arrangement uses c/c600, so its framing dimensions are not claimed as the adopted recipe. Joist sizing, supports, spans, connectors and structural verification remain project details.
attic_defaults.materials: Historic wool conductivity0.04W/(mK), density29kg/m³ and specific heat1030J/(kgK), and the shared softwood and lining properties are unchanged. The renovation states retain all original layers and add the accepted200/500mm loose wool at conductivity0.037W/(mK). Thin air/vapour control and wind protection, ventilation and moisture design remain project details; this nominal model does not certify code compliance.
